title: Penetration Test Report
subtitle: AASTAR Price Dashboard
meta: Branch SIT. Before fixes: f127d70 (+ 1dc6a24). After fixes: eb0225b

Isolated local QA copy: API 127.0.0.1:8710 with APP_ENV=prod, frontend localhost:5181, throwaway PostgreSQL 18 (port 5546) with the production role layout, demo prices from 2024 and synthetic Google-Sheet data; integrations off
Claude Code (prod-readiness-checks), for the AASTAR project team
Low residual risk after fixes: 0 Critical/High; 2 Medium found and fixed; 3 Low accepted or open (decision on HTTPS)

blocks.p: An authorized grey-box penetration test of the dashboard, requested by its owner, ahead of the first production release. Active tests ran only against the isolated local QA copy; the staging server received about 24 passive, unauthenticated GET/HEAD requests. Real integrations, other applications and the production hosts were out of scope.

blocks.note: Overall risk: Low. Access control, sessions, CSRF, injection, uploads, SSRF and SSO all held. The remaining exposure depends on deployment: run production over its own hostname, and HTTPS as soon as possible.

bullets: **Active (local QA copy):** frontend localhost:5181 and API 127.0.0.1:8710 with APP_ENV=prod; throwaway PostgreSQL 18; fixtures prefixed qa-pt-.
**Passive (staging):** http://172.28.92.56:3170 - unauthenticated GET/HEAD only, no logins, no payloads; the backend host was never contacted directly.

**Coverage:** OWASP Top 10 2021 / ASVS - authentication, vertical and horizontal authorization, mass assignment, SQL and header injection, CSV injection, uploads, stored XSS, CSRF/Origin, SSRF, headers and errors, rate limiting, OIDC (code review), secrets in git history, dependencies, container and proxy hardening.
**Tools:** qa/pentest/pentest-suite.mjs (Node), qa/stack/rate_limit_check.py, npm audit, git log searches, source review.
**Limits:** no load or DoS tests; SSO by code review (disabled locally); Python dependencies reviewed against known CVEs because pip-audit is not installed.

rows: CSV/formula injection in the audit-log export, injectable without signing in
Staging exposes API docs (APP_ENV=sit) and version details without a session
AI reports and News documents are shared between users of the module
No Secure cookie flag on plain-HTTP origins

blocks.p: **PT-INJ-04 - CSV / formula injection (CVSS 3.1 6.1, AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:R/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:N)**

Description and impact: The audit CSV export wrote cells as stored. A failed sign-in records the typed e-mail verbatim, so an anonymous visitor could plant "=HYPERLINK(...)" that runs when an administrator opens the export.
Proof (redacted): Unauthenticated POST /api/auth/login with email "=2+5+qapt<run>", then the admin export contained the cell unescaped.
Fix and re-test: core/csvsafe.py prefixes text starting with = + - @ TAB CR with a quote in both CSV exports; numbers (negative spreads) stay numeric. Test tests/test_csv_safety.py. Re-test: SECURE.
**PT-DEP-01 - react-router-dom 6.28.0**
Description and impact: npm audit: 3 high advisories (GHSA-2w69-qvjg-hvjx, GHSA-2j2x-hqr9-3h42).
Proof (redacted): npm audit --omit=dev.

Fix and re-test: Upgraded to 6.30.6. Two moderate advisories remain that only React Router 7 fixes: one concerns server-side rendering (not used); the other, a backslash open redirect, is closed in the app - the sign-in "next" check now refuses backslashes, like the server-side check. Re-test: no high advisories.
**PT-CFG-02/04/05 - information disclosure on staging**

Description and impact: Staging runs APP_ENV=sit, which enables /api/docs and /api/openapi.json; /api/auth/config and /api/health/ready return environment, release and migration revision without a session.
Proof (redacted): Passive GETs on http://172.28.92.56:3170.
Fix and re-test: Accepted for staging (internal). Production runs APP_ENV=prod, where the docs answer 404 (verified on the QA copy).
**PT-AC-07 - shared AI reports and documents**

Description and impact: Any user holding ai_analysis can read any AI report by id and the list shows requester e-mails; News documents likewise. The module guard holds (a viewer without the module gets 403).
Proof (redacted): Report created by one analyst read by another.
Fix and re-test: Accepted as the intended shared analyst desk - confirm with the product owner; scope by requested_by if isolation is wanted.
**PT-AUTH-04 - cookies without Secure on HTTP**
Description and impact: Secure is set only when APP_BASE_URL is https. Over plain HTTP the session token travels in cleartext and, on a shared IP, reaches every other app on that IP.
Proof (redacted): Set-Cookie on the QA copy: HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax, no Secure.
Fix and re-test: Open, tied to architecture finding AR-04: an own hostname for production from day one and HTTPS as soon as a certificate exists.

bullets: Security headers present: CSP, X-Frame-Options DENY, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, COOP, Permissions-Policy; server version hidden; API responses no-store.
Protected endpoints answer 401 without a session.
/.env and /.git/config return the SPA page (fallback), not files - false positives.

Information disclosure while staging runs APP_ENV=sit: /api/docs and /api/openapi.json (62 paths), environment, release and migration revision on /api/auth/config and /api/health/ready (PT-CFG-02/04/05).
The CSP allows the HTTP staging Hub; production must use the HTTPS Hub.

Authentication: generic errors, no user enumeration (equal timing via a dummy Argon2id hash), lockout, fresh session on sign-in, server-side logout, sessions revoked on password change and when a user is disabled, sign-in rate limit (10/min).
Authorization: admin APIs refused to analysts and viewers, no self-escalation or mass assignment, data.export and pipeline.run enforced, module checks on every series and section.
Injection: bound parameters everywhere; probes on every query and path parameter returned 404/422 without SQL errors; Content-Disposition names sanitised.
CSRF: session-bound double-submit token and Origin allow-list (now also required when Origin is missing).
Uploads: type and size checks per route, admin-only (News: documents.upload).
XSS: React escaping, no dangerouslySetInnerHTML, Markdown without raw HTML; strict CSP.
SSRF: Google sheet IDs fixed in code; the service-account token endpoint is constant.
SSO (code review): single-use hashed state, nonce, PKCE S256, JWKS-verified tokens with an algorithm allow-list, safe redirects.
Secrets: none in git history; .env files ignored. Containers run as non-root; source maps removed.
Serve production on its own hostname from day one and over HTTPS as soon as a certificate is available (PT-AUTH-04 / AR-04).
Keep APP_ENV=prod in production; consider trimming release and environment from the unauthenticated /api/auth/config.
Confirm that shared AI reports and documents are intended (PT-AC-07).
Plan the React Router 7 upgrade to clear the two remaining moderate advisories.

blocks.p: **How to re-run:**

blocks.code:
backend/.venv/Scripts/python qa/stack/make_env.py        # throwaway settings (gitignored backend/.env.qa)
backend/.venv/Scripts/python qa/stack/pg_cluster.py start # PostgreSQL 18 on 127.0.0.1:5546
backend/.venv/Scripts/python qa/stack/setup_db.py         # migrate, bootstrap, demo prices, sheet data
preview: aastar-qa-api (port 8710) + aastar-web (port 5181)  # .claude/launch.json
node qa/functional/api-suite.mjs
node qa/pentest/pentest-suite.mjs
backend/.venv/Scripts/python qa/stack/rate_limit_check.py # the real 10/min sign-in limit
cd backend && MIGRATION_DATABASE_URL=<QA owner URL>/postgres .venv/Scripts/python -m pytest -q
